pointers.sentence: It calls `BaseDatabaseWrapper.prepare_database`, a hook, empty in the base class, for a backend with a database to check or prepare first, and makes the executor, whose loader builds the graph from the migration files and reads which migrations are applied (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`, `django/db/backends/base/base.py:BaseDatabaseWrapper.prepare_database`).

It calls `BaseDatabaseWrapper.prepare_database`, a hook, empty in the base class, for a backend with a database to check or prepare first, and makes the executor, whose loader builds the graph from the migration files and reads which migrations are applied (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`, `django/db/backends/base/base.py:BaseDatabaseWrapper.prepare_database`).

`MigrationLoader.detect_conflicts` returns the applications with more than one leaf node (a migration on which no other migration of the application depends), and for any the command raises `CommandError` and names the remedy ([The makemigrations command](makemigrations.md)) (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`).

A migration that replaces others, a squashed one, may stand in the graph in their place; while only some of them are applied it is left out, and a name that finds it gives the last of the migrations it replaces as the target ([Squashed migrations: `replaces` and the squashmigrations command](squashing.md)) (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`).
`--prune`, `--plan` and `--check` each end migrate before anything is applied (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`).

`--plan` prints the plan: each migration, and under it a line for each of its operations from `Command.describe_operation`, which says IRREVERSIBLE where a `RunPython` or a `RunSQL` is to run backwards and was given nothing to run (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.describe_operation`).
`emit_pre_migrate_signal` sends `pre_migrate` once for each application of the main registry that has a models module (`django/core/management/sql.py:emit_pre_migrate_signal`).

The executor reports each migration to `Command.migration_progress_callback`, which prints its line, at verbosity 2 with the time it took and at verbosity 0 not at all (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.migration_progress_callback`).
The state the executor returns is changed before `post_migrate` is sent, since a receiver may ask its registry for any model (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`).

`ProjectState.clear_delayed_apps_cache` discards a registry that an operation re-rendered only in part, the models near its change and not those further off, so that the next read renders every model state afresh (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.clear_delayed_apps_cache`).
Django's reference tells a receiver to take its models from apps (`docs/ref/signals.txt`).

Django connects one receiver to `pre_migrate`, `inject_rename_contenttypes_operations`, whose work is to put an operation of its own after each `RenameModel` in the migrations of the plan it is handed, for the executor to run ([Content types, static files and the other contrib apps](../contrib.md)) (`django/contrib/contenttypes/management/__init__.py:inject_rename_contenttypes_operations`).

To `post_migrate`, contenttypes connects `create_contenttypes`, auth `create_permissions` and `rename_permissions_after_model_rename` ([Authentication, sessions and messages](../auth.md)), and sites `create_default_site` (`django/contrib/contenttypes/apps.py:ContentTypesConfig.ready`, `django/contrib/auth/apps.py:AuthConfig.ready`, `django/contrib/sites/apps.py:SitesConfig.ready`).

To `post_migrate`, contenttypes connects `create_contenttypes`, auth `create_permissions` and `rename_permissions_after_model_rename` ([Authentication, sessions and messages](../auth.md)), and sites `create_default_site` (`django/contrib/contenttypes/apps.py:ContentTypesConfig.ready`, `django/contrib/auth/apps.py:AuthConfig.ready`, `django/contrib/sites/apps.py:SitesConfig.ready`).

To `post_migrate`, contenttypes connects `create_contenttypes`, auth `create_permissions` and `rename_permissions_after_model_rename` ([Authentication, sessions and messages](../auth.md)), and sites `create_default_site` (`django/contrib/contenttypes/apps.py:ContentTypesConfig.ready`, `django/contrib/auth/apps.py:AuthConfig.ready`, `django/contrib/sites/apps.py:SitesConfig.ready`).

Before the executor, unless verbosity is 0, the command then looks for changes in the models that no migration has: an autodetector, of the class in `Command.autodetector`, is given the loader's `MigrationLoader.project_state` as its from-state and `ProjectState.from_apps` of the main registry as its to-state, and a notice names the applications in what its `MigrationAutodetector.changes` returns, if anything ([The autodetector: comparing two project states](autodetector.md)) (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`).

`Command.sync_apps` reads the names of the tables the database has, asks `ConnectionRouter.get_migratable_models` for each application's models, sets aside those whose table is there, and in one schema editor calls `BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor.create_model` for each of the rest that `Options.can_migrate` allows (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.sync_apps`, `django/db/models/options.py:Options.can_migrate`).

`Command.sync_apps` reads the names of the tables the database has, asks `ConnectionRouter.get_migratable_models` for each application's models, sets aside those whose table is there, and in one schema editor calls `BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor.create_model` for each of the rest that `Options.can_migrate` allows (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.sync_apps`, `django/db/models/options.py:Options.can_migrate`).
So yard's tables, whose foreign keys name fleet's, were made first, which Django's documentation says may work and is not supported (`docs/topics/migrations.txt`).

`Command.get_check_kwargs` gives the alias to the system checks that run first, so that the checks kept for databases run, for that alias alone ([The system checks](../commands/checks.md)) (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.get_check_kwargs`).

An operation on a model or a field that changes a table asks it, in its database half, whether the model belongs on the connection, and sends nothing where it does not ([Operations: the base class and its two halves](operations.md), [Routing between databases: `ConnectionRouter`](../backends/routers.md)) (`django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation.allow_migrate_model`).
showmigrations has two listings (`django/core/management/commands/showmigrations.py:Command.handle`).

The default, `--list`, is by application: `Command.show_list` prints the nodes of each application named, or else of every migrated one, in the order of the `MigrationGraph.forwards_plan` of its leaf nodes, and marks each by two readings of what is applied, the loader's and, apart from it, a recorder's `MigrationRecorder.applied_migrations` (`django/core/management/commands/showmigrations.py:Command.show_list`).

`Command.show_plan` takes the forwards plan of every leaf node, or of the leaf nodes of the applications named, keeps each node once, and marks it `"[X]"` where its key is in the loader's `MigrationLoader.applied_migrations` (`django/core/management/commands/showmigrations.py:Command.show_plan`).
sqlmigrate prints the statements one migration would send (`django/core/management/commands/sqlmigrate.py:Command.handle`).

`collect_sql` has the migration apply or unapply itself, from the state of the migrations it depends on, whatever the database has had, to a schema editor whose `BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor.execute` keeps each statement it is handed as text in place of sending it ([Finding migrations: `MigrationLoader`](loader.md)) (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.collect_sql`, `django/db/backends/base/schema.py:BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor.execute`).

`collect_sql` has the migration apply or unapply itself, from the state of the migrations it depends on, whatever the database has had, to a schema editor whose `BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor.execute` keeps each statement it is handed as text in place of sending it ([Finding migrations: `MigrationLoader`](loader.md)) (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.collect_sql`, `django/db/backends/base/schema.py:BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor.execute`).

`Migration.apply` and `Migration.unapply`, told to collect, write a comment naming each operation, as in the lines printed here, and another in place of calling the database half of a `RunPython`, whose `RunPython.reduces_to_sql` is false (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.apply`).

`"BEGIN;"` and `"COMMIT;"` are not statements the editor collected: `BaseCommand.execute` writes the string that `handle` returns, and where the command's `BaseCommand.output_transaction` is true puts the connection's `BaseDatabaseOperations.start_transaction_sql` and `BaseDatabaseOperations.end_transaction_sql` around it (`django/core/management/base.py:BaseCommand.execute`). sqlmigrate sets the attribute for each run: true where the migration's `Migration.atomic` is true and the features have `BaseDatabaseFeatures.can_rollback_ddl`, as SQLite's do.
